Standard: The anticollision light system consists of one or more approved anticollision lights located so that their light will not impair the flight crew’s vision or detract from the conspicuity of the position lights. The system will consist of enough lights to illuminate the vital areas around the air vehicle. For fixed-wing air vehicles, the field of coverage extends in each direction within at least 75 degrees above and 75 degrees below the horizontal plane of the air vehicle, except that there may be solid angles of obstructed visibility totaling not more than 0.5 steradians. For rotary-wing air vehicles, the field of coverage extends in each direction within at least 30 degrees above and 30 degrees below the horizontal plane of the air vehicle, except that there may be solid angles of obstructed visibility totaling not more than 0.5 steradians. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Anticollision light locations are verified by examining drawings, digital mockups, or the physical air vehicle. Analysis.
  (1) Light beam spread and overlap is verified by analysis.
